base_changes.content: In repo /stand/ws (ship-cost), scripts/cost.sh fails with `no rate for zone "north"` on data/zone-rates.tsv because that file is a spreadsheet export with CRLF line endings: awk splits on tab only, so zone keys keep a trailing \r and never match the LF-ended orders file. Workaround without editing the files: `tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/rates.tsv` and pass it as the second argument. Permanent fix would be `tr -d '\r'` on input or `,` handling inside cost.sh.

record.final_answer:
Total shipping cost for October: **58.01**

Per-order output from scripts/cost.sh:

    A-1001  north    6.94
    A-1002  south    6.28
    A-1003  island  15.25
    A-1004  north   15.10
    A-1005  south    9.03
    A-1006  north    5.41
    total           58.01

One catch you should know about: the script as-is does not work on this data. `data/zone-rates.tsv` was exported from a spreadsheet with CRLF line endings, but the awk in `scripts/cost.sh:7-9` splits only on tab, so the rate table's zone keys come back as `north\r`, `south\r`, `island\r` and never match the LF-only zone names in the orders file:

    cost.sh: no rate for zone "north" (order A-1001)   (exit 1)

Since you asked me not to touch the script or the rate card, I passed a de-CRLF'd copy via the script's optional second argument (`$rates`), which is exactly the 58.01 above. I re-computed the same figures independently in Python with exact decimals and got identical numbers, so the total is right and the failure is purely the line-ending mismatch. Both repo files are untouched (`git status` clean).

If you want a permanent fix later, the cleanest options are `tr -d '\r'` when reading the rates file in `cost.sh`, or having the logistics export write LF — say the word and I'll patch the script.
